 Pinned Updated   Nov. 12, 2026, 11:20 a.m. ET Sharon Otterman Sarah Chatta Ana Ley Rachel Sherman and Max Bearak 
 Here’s the latest. 
 The death toll in the Brooklyn apartment building collapse rose to at least eight on Thursday, Mayor Zohran Mamdani said, as emergency workers continued to search through the rubble in search of possible survivors.
 At least 17 people were injured, including three firefighters, the mayor said. At least four of the injured were in critical condition, the Fire Department said in a statement earlier Thursday.
 The three-story building collapsed at 1321 Flatbush Avenue in the Flatbush neighborhood just after 4 p.m. on Wednesday, falling into a hole created by a construction site at a neighboring lot.
 The building contained four apartments, with a commercial space on the ground floor, according to city information. Seven children were among those injured, officials said.
 The rescue operation, which was still underway late Thursday morning, involved canine units, drones, helicopters and fire trucks alongside excavation machinery. The wall of an adjacent building was sheared off by the collapse, leaving a staircase, bedrooms and closets exposed to the elements.
 Mr. Mamdani said that the Department of Buildings and law enforcement would lead an investigation into the cause of the collapse.
 “There are no words for a loss of this magnitude,” Mr. Mamdani said on social media on Thursday. “My heart is with the families and loved ones of those we have lost, those who are injured and everyone grieving today.”
 The Department of Buildings said the developers of the construction site adjacent to the collapsed building had an active permit for excavation and foundation work on the lot. The city’s buildings commissioner, Ahmed Tigani, told reporters that workers had been excavating it at the time of the collapse. A full stop-work order has been issued for the site.
 There were still people on the sidewalk Thursday morning, looking on in the hope of news.
 “We don’t know anything,” said Leonor Yupa, as she watched responders haul debris out of the construction site where her 22-year-old son, Gabriel Siguencia, had started working as a carpenter two weeks ago. 
 She and her husband had not heard from him since news broke of the collapse, she said.
 Here’s what else to know:
 Street closures: Flatbush Avenue was closed from Clarendon Road to Bedford Avenue. Officials asked people to avoid the area. Water mains near the site of the collapse were also shut down.
 The building: The collapsed apartment building had been home to a number of businesses over the decades, including a medical clothes store and a tax-services office, according to city records. Read more › 
 Nearby site: A one-story building used to occupy the construction site next to the collapse. In March, the Department of Buildings ordered the property owner to halt demolition work after it found that there was inadequate protection for nearby properties. The order was fully lifted in August after the department found that the project team had corrected the violations.
 Show more Nov. 12, 2026, 11:16 a.m. ET Wesley Parnell 
 Diego Sandoval, Mexico’s consul for protection affairs, and other Mexican officials have been at the scene since early this morning. Sandoval said the Mexican government was in touch with the city of New York and ready to facilitate diplomatic connections for any foreign nationals from Latin America who may have been hurt. The neighborhood is home to many immigrants and construction tends to draw Latin American workers. “Up until this point, we haven’t identified any Mexican nationals, but we stand ready,” Sandoval said. 
 Nov. 12, 2026, 11:05 a.m. ET Wesley Parnell 
 Yolanda Solomon, 48, a local pastor in the Flatbush area, said that her Brooklyn community had been concerned about the pace and safety of construction projects amid rapid gentrification and development. “I know a lot of people are not a fan of the new construction,” she said.
 “I think that people are a little wary when you have buildings going up so quickly,” she added. “Hopefully, the mayor’s office will do a thorough investigation.”

 Nov. 12, 2026, 10:58 a.m. ET Nate Schweber 
 Benewaa Bonsu, a longtime resident along Flatbush Avenue, said she had been walking by the construction zone an hour before the collapse on Wednesday and was startled to hear loud pops. “I thought it was gunshots at first,” she said. She could not see into the construction zone but could hear workers’ voices inside. When she sensed no alarm, she kept moving. An hour later, friends reached out asking if she was OK. She dashed out of her building, saw the wreckage and wondered if it had anything to do with the pops she heard.
 Nov. 12, 2026, 10:44 a.m. ET Mihir Zaveri 
 An inspection of the construction site, commissioned by the contractors and filed with the Department of Buildings in March, noted that the north facade of the collapsed building — 1321 Flatbush Avenue — was in “poor condition with noticeable cracks.” The construction site is to the north of the of the collapsed building.
 Nov. 12, 2026, 10:42 a.m. ET Mihir Zaveri 
 Records filed with the Buildings Department show that a special inspector — essentially a third party that is supposed to verify that work is being done correctly — was supposed to be overseeing foundation work at the construction site adjacent to the collapsed building. But, according to city records, that special inspector’s license expired in July. It’s unclear whether that person was still working for the contractors or was on site, and the Buildings Department did not immediately clarify.
 Nov. 12, 2026, 10:39 a.m. ET Wesley Parnell 
 While visiting the Flatbush YMCA, which has been used as a staging site for aid groups and a temporary shelter, the Brooklyn Borough president, Antonio Reynoso, said that the city was laser focused on helping victims, particularly those in critical condition. An investigation was in the works. “Our focus is seeing what we can do to help the families that have lost someone, but also the ones that are in critical condition, whether we can move them to stable condition,” Reynoso said. “That’s the work that we’re already doing now. Thereafter, we’ll talk about what caused this, how it happened, who to hold accountable.”
 Nov. 12, 2026, 10:25 a.m. ET Sally Goldenberg 
 Mayor Zohran Mamdani is scheduled to hold a news conference at noon today at the site of the building collapse to provide updates on the situation there, said Dora Pekec, his spokeswoman. The mayor will be joined by officials from the Fire Department.
 Nov. 12, 2026, 10:02 a.m. ET Emma Fitzsimmons 
 Rodneyse Bichotte Hermelyn, a state assemblywoman has an office across from the site of the collapse. She said she had been helping families and first responders in the heavily immigrant neighborhood over the last day. 
 She said some victims were construction workers and others were residents of the buildings. She saw a toddler pulled from the rubble and a pregnant woman whose husband was searching for her. “That was very emotional,” she said. “We were praying for him and hugging him.” She said the toddler was transported to the hospital. 
 Nov. 12, 2026, 9:51 a.m. ET Kaja Andric 
 A woman lifted her hands in prayer as she stared at the collapsed building. “Show us your mercy, Lord,” she repeated.

 Excavation work was taking place next to the building that collapsed, officials say. 
 Image Firefighters working in the rubble of the collapsed building, which had largely fallen into the open construction pit next door, in Brooklyn on Thursday. Credit... Dave Sanders for The New York Times New York City officials ordered construction at a Brooklyn site to be halted after an apartment building collapsed onto it, killing eight people.
 Hundreds of firefighters worked through the night, sifting through the rubble of the collapsed building, which had largely fallen into the open construction pit next door.
 Building officials said plans for a three-story building had been approved for the site, and that developers had submitted plans for a nine-story building. Excavation work was taking place at the site at the time of the collapse, officials said. Previously, the plot had been home to a one-story building.
 Mayor Zohran Mamdani said that the Department of Buildings and law enforcement officials would lead an investigation into the cause of the collapse. “This has been an incredibly challenging and fast-moving situation with precarious wreckage to navigate and dangerous voids beneath the surface,” he told reporters.
 A full stop-work order was issued for the construction site, the department said, adding that its engineers were conducting structural stability inspections of nearby buildings.
 A statement from the Department of Buildings added that its inspectors and engineers were at the site of the collapse and that the department had also launched an investigation, in tandem with law enforcement officials.
 The department said the developers of the construction site adjacent to the collapsed building had an active permit for excavation and foundation work on the lot.
 In March, the Department of Buildings ordered the property owner at the construction site to halt demolition work after it found that there was inadequate protection for nearby properties. The order was fully lifted in August after the department found that the project team had corrected the violations.

 The city’s Department of Environmental Protection said that it had shut down city water mains near the site of the collapse so that emergency crews could continue search and rescue operations. About 100 buildings are affected.
 Nov. 12, 2026, 9:18 a.m. ET Miles Cohen 
 Leonor Yupa and her husband, Ramon Yupa, draped in a blanket, had been waiting on a sidewalk across from the collapsed building since 8 p.m on Wednesday night, waiting for information about their 22-year-old son, Gabriel Siguencia, a carpenter at the construction site next door.
 “We don’t know anything,” Leonor Yupa said as she watched responders haul debris out of the site where their son started working two weeks ago. They have not heard from him since news broke of the collapse.

 Fire officials are planning to hold a news briefing to update New Yorkers on the building collapse between 11 a.m. and noon, according a Fire Department spokesperson. 
 Nov. 12, 2026, 9:07 a.m. ET Emma Fitzsimmons 
 Farah Louis, a City Council member who represents the neighborhood, called for an “immediate, thorough, and transparent investigation into the structural failure and the building’s compliance history.”
 “Our Flatbush community is grieving an unimaginable tragedy,” she said in a statement. “Lives were lost, neighbors were injured, and families have been shaken to their core.“
 Nov. 12, 2026, 8:47 a.m. ET Kaja Andric 
 A team of excavators sifted through floorboards, drywall and pink wall insulation with picks and shovels on Thursday morning, releasing clouds of smoke. Nearby, children wearing backpacks on their way to school walked past news cameras filming the scene. 
 Video Credit Credit... Bing Guan for The New York Times Nov. 12, 2026, 8:40 a.m. ET Troy Closson 
 It was striking how quiet Flatbush Ave. was around 8:30 a.m. on the blocks around of the building collapse site. But at the scene, several dozen people watched alongside news cameras as emergency workers continued to dig through the rubble. “This is the aftermath,” one woman said as she walked by filming on her iPhone.
 Image Credit... Bing Guan for The New York Times Nov. 12, 2026, 8:39 a.m. ET Mihir Zaveri 
 At the construction site next door to the collapse, developers were working to build a nine-story, mixed-use building with 64 apartments, a community space and a grocery store, according to plans filed with the City Planning Commission earlier this week.
 Nov. 12, 2026, 8:29 a.m. ET Kaja Andric 
 A woman was just carried out of Bethesda Church of God in Christ, collapsing as she wept in front of the church. Two people picked her up and carried her away as she screamed “I can’t” in Spanish.
 Nov. 12, 2026, 8:09 a.m. ET Hurubie Meko 
 Eric Gonzalez, the Brooklyn district attorney, said his office is working closely with the city’s Department of Buildings and other law enforcement agencies to “determine whether any criminal conduct contributed” to yesterday’s building collapse in Flatbush that has led to at least eight deaths. “I am heartbroken by the tragic loss of life,” Mr. Gonzalez said.

 Rain expected around noon could complicate the rescue efforts, Kavanagh said. “Rain can flood those voids where they are still searching and destabilize the ground they are on. The crews this morning are certainly aware of it and working to complete as much of the search as they can before the rain starts.”

 The neighboring building, whose walls are now partially torn off, offers a surreal view inside several apartments. In one, an entire closet is exposed, revealing a line of jackets and shirts, bags piled on top of each other below. In another, what appears to be a bed is covered in pink sheets, a mound of clothes sitting on top. 
 Image Credit... Dave Sanders for The New York Times Nov. 12, 2026, 7:57 a.m. ET Emma Fitzsimmons 
 Laura Kavanagh, the city’s former fire commissioner, said in an interview that the death toll was likely higher because so many people were at home on the Veterans Day holiday. 
 Nov. 12, 2026, 6:22 a.m. ET Rachel Sherman and Max Bearak 
 Dozens wait near the collapsed building, hoping for news. 
 Image Emergency responders at the scene of a building collapse in Brooklyn on Thursday. Credit... Bing Guan for The New York Times Hundreds of New York City firefighters sifted through the rubble of a collapsed apartment building early Thursday as dozens of onlookers, including family members of the building’s residents, gathered.
 Among them were Abubakar Diallo and his nephew Habib N’Diaye, who were growing frustrated as Mr. N’Diaye waited for updates on his younger brother.
 “We called 311, they don’t have any information. We called the hospital, they don’t have anything,” said Mr. Diallo, 47.
 Mr. N’Diaye, 32, lived in the three-story apartment building that collapsed on Wednesday afternoon. He said he was waiting for information on his brother, Mamadou Bhoye N’Diaye, 31, and their relative, Mamadou Bhoye Barry, 23.
 Sirens blared and drones hovered overhead well past midnight in Brooklyn’s Flatbush neighborhood. The collapsed building had taken down the wall of an adjacent building with it, exposing the interior of its apartments to the open air.
 The collapsed building largely fell into a neighboring plot that was a construction site. It was in that pit that around 250 firefighters worked through the night.
 Emmanuella Carilus, 32, who has lived in the neighborhood for 12 years, was still taking in all that had happened. “I was shocked, I was shook,” she said while on a late-night walk. “I live literally right behind the building. It sounded like a big boom, and you just heard a bunch of screaming,” she said, describing the moment the building collapsed at around 4 p.m. on Wednesday.
 She said she was praying for anyone who was trapped and their loved ones and that she was concerned about the effects of the dust from the collapse on her neighborhood.
 Fire officials said that they did not know how many people might be missing and that the search operation was likely to continue for days.
